fieldNotes.location: Roster geocode (44.60417,-123.935516, address 1 Butler Bridge Rd) sat in the Yaquina River / treatment-pond area south of the actual mill - imprecise. Mill relocated via satellite and web research to the GP Toledo Mill complex on a peninsula on the east bank of the Yaquina River, ~44.6145,-123.9370. Confirmed address: 1400 SE Butler Bridge Rd, Toledo, OR 97391.
fieldNotes.facility: Georgia-Pacific Toledo Mill - an integrated kraft pulp and linerboard (containerboard) mill operating since 1957; makes linerboard for corrugated boxes from virgin wood chips and recycled fiber. GP also operates the Juno recycling technology facility on-site. Subject of the Infor Phase 2 dossier item. Compact, water-bound campus: paper-machine and process buildings, chemical recovery, large chip pile, woodyard with conveyors, finished-goods warehouses along the riverfront, trailer drop yards, rail yard, and a private Butler Bridge linking to west-bank facilities (additional warehouses / log storage).
fieldNotes.truckGate: TRUE - controlled mill entrance. The site is fully enclosed by perimeter chain-link/mesh fencing (visible in Street View, 2024-07, all along SE Butler Bridge Rd) with a rail spur separating the public road from the yard. All truck traffic funnels through one controlled entrance; a guarded/scaled checkpoint is universal for an integrated kraft pulp/linerboard mill receiving chip and recycled-fiber vans.
fieldNotes.guardShack: TRUE (medium confidence) - a small building cluster sits at the yard entrance area near 44.6165,-123.9372, consistent with a guard/scale house. Not pinpointed at high resolution - flagged. (Note: a separate white shed on the road shoulder with a 'City of Toledo' sign is a city utility building, not the mill gate.)
fieldNotes.preGateStaging: Paved staging/parking areas along SE Butler Bridge Rd hold queued semis (Street View shows trucks staged there).
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved yard inside the gate before the docks; trailers staged on the entrance loop road.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Internal roads (the curved entrance loop plus the access road past the chip pile) easily hold a queue of 3+ trucks.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Site is constrained between the river and the rail line; limited unused paved width for a dedicated bypass lane - left true at low confidence given the wide entrance loop, flagged.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Receiving (chip/recycled-fiber vans to the woodyard, rail receiving) is physically separate from finished-linerboard shipping at the riverfront warehouses - distinct clusters.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Finished-goods warehouses along the SW riverfront show dock-door banks; counted band 10-25 (~14 estimated), medium confidence (roof shadow / resolution).
fieldNotes.dropArea: Extensive trailer drop yards: rows of dozens of parked trailers along the curved entrance loop and the eastern yard - well over 50 trailers visible, band 50+.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus: pulp/paper process core, chemical recovery, chip pile and woodyard, multiple riverfront warehouses, rail yard, the Juno recycling facility, plus west-bank facilities across the private Butler Bridge - 18+ distinct structures.
fieldNotes.railServed: TRUE - rail spurs run directly along and into the property; rail cars (boxcars) visible parked at the yard frontage in both satellite and Street View.
fieldNotes.scale: TRUE (medium confidence) - truck scales for chip/fiber van weigh-in are operationally required at an integrated kraft mill; a scale-house-sized structure sits in the truck path near the gate. Not resolved precisely - flagged.
fieldNotes.multiStep: Possible gate-then-scale sequence but not clearly confirmed - left false, flagged.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Toledo is a small Oregon town (~3,500 people) on the central Oregon coast; the mill is on a peninsula at the edge of town surrounded by the Yaquina River and forest. Rural.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~230 acres for the full fenced industrial property including east-bank mill core, warehouses, woodyard, drop yards and west-bank facilities; honest estimate from the perimeter box.

verification.rationale: GP-owned containerboard mill, operating; named Cedar Springs volume recipient. Demand-driven temporary layoffs reported, not permanent closure.
